gap: None of the results ChatGPT got normalise '65W' across the alternatives it named. Once a second device is plugged in, the laptop port drops to 45 W on the UGREEN, the D-Link DCP-651 and the Verbatim 32201 alike, but the phone port differs: 20 W on the UGREEN and D-Link, 18 W on the Verbatim. With all three ports in use, the Verbatim's total falls to 60 W and the UGREEN's to 62 W, while the D-Link's stays at 65 W.
standout_why: I checked the rival pages I could open: smartgadgetkit.com (UGREEN review), en.best-batteries.com (UGREEN review), mobileplustech.com, wattapick.com and themacspecialist.uk. All of them, and ChatGPT's own answers, already give the UGREEN's 45 + 20 W split, and smartgadgetkit and Best Batteries also give its 8.5 W three-port figure. So the UGREEN half of the finding is not new. None of these pages gives the split for the Verbatim 32201 or the D-Link DCP-651, even though ChatGPT recommended both. Wattapick goes further and says 'UGREEN does not publish the power split'. Androidcentral (the cited rival) and thisusb could not be read: one returned only its title, the other failed on its SSL certificate. CNA and CN Traveller were not opened.
decides: This confirms the UGREEN pick rather than changing it. The '65W is shared, so the laptop drops to about 45 W' caveat that ChatGPT attaches only to the UGREEN applies equally to the D-Link and the Verbatim. On the published splits the Verbatim is slightly worse: 18 W to the second USB-C port against 20 W, and 60 W in total with three devices against 62 W. The D-Link alone keeps the full 65 W with three devices connected, but D-Link's page only says it is 'compatible' with AU/EU/UK/US standards and does not say which plug heads are in the box. A shopper charging a laptop and a phone gets the same 45 W to the laptop whichever of these three they buy.
